GitHub issue body contract evidence, retrieved 2026-11-21.
Source excerpts are distinguished from deductions and limits below.

Closing references
https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue
The documented closing keywords are:
"close", "closes", "closed", "fix", "fixes", "fixed", "resolve", "resolves", "resolved".
They apply in a PR description or commit message for a default-branch merge.
Deduction: `Parent: https://github.com/<repo>/issues/<n>` does not contain a
closing keyword. This header alone does not close the parent when a child's
PR merges. Separate explicit closing references or manual PR links still can.

Body strings through gh (v2.102.0)
https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/v2.102.0/pkg/cmd/api/fields.go
Raw fields bypass magicFieldValue; the literal body string is retained.
https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/v2.102.0/pkg/cmd/api/http.go
Non-GET map parameters are serialized with json.Marshal(pp), preserving the
string value in the request JSON (line endings are escaped on the wire).
https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/v2.102.0/api/queries_issue.go
The Issue struct stores the fetched body in a Go string: `Body string`.
https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/v2.102.0/pkg/cmd/issue/view/view.go
For --json, viewRun returns `opts.Exporter.Write(opts.IO, issue)` rather than
using the Markdown renderer.
https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/v2.102.0/pkg/cmdutil/json_flags.go
The exporter encodes selected fields using encoding/json:
`encoder.Encode(e.exportData(reflect.ValueOf(data)))`.
Deduction: gh's JSON path preserves LF or CRLF in the decoded body string;
JSON output bytes themselves contain escapes, not literal embedded newlines.

Observed counterexample to assuming all fetched bodies use LF
https://api.github.com/repos/cli/cli/issues/5680
The read-only REST response retrieved on 2026-11-21 has CRLF throughout its
body, including the first separator, represented by `\r\n\r\n` in JSON.
This establishes that CRLF bodies exist; it does not establish how this issue
was authored. The capture is summarized here without copying its prose.

Scope correction for the carried LF/idempotency claim
No live REST-write/gh-view round trip was performed. The sources above support
gh's string transport, not a universal server-side byte-preservation guarantee
or a claim about the origin of CRLF. The old inference that byte-exact
startswith(header) suffices is withdrawn. Reconciliation must recognize an
existing header with LF or CRLF and leave the original body untouched. The
FakeGitHub rerun regression exercises that behavior, including no body update.
